correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly handles all \(m\ge1\), nonzero rational \((a,b)\), primitive roots of each dyadic order, endpoint characters, and kernel normalization. At primitive order \(\ge4\), invertible rational recursion matrices reduce any nonzero rational combination to a nonzero polynomial of degree below the irreducible 2-power cyclotomic polynomial. Exact endpoint evaluations then show at most one possible zero. The irrational real counterexample is evaluated symbolically at an eighth root. The standalone standard-library checker confirms 576 integer mixing pairs at 12 levels, 3168 exact cyclotomic remainder tests and 24 independent exact circulant ranks. Finite tests are corroborative, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact rational-parameter, all-depth cyclic-convolution rank-and-kernel classification and its sharp failure for real irrational mixes are not consequences of the inspected norm, wavelet, or orthogonal-transform results. The 1976 quoted theorem treats odd-order roots, while this theorem excludes dyadic primitive zeros. published-finding corpus and previously recorded results were compared at the level of implications. The inaccessible 1976 full text remains a genuine priority risk; this is same-model assessment, not independent proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Historical original article Brillhart–Lomont–Morton (1976) could have an uninspected dyadic-root corollary beyond the odd-root Theorem 6.1 cited in accessible 2019 full text; full article inaccessible.
2007 orthogonal-transform and 2011 wavelet article full texts were not completely accessible. Their inspected statements do not imply the result, but no full-text exclusion is asserted.
A generic result elsewhere on rational linear independence of Rudin–Shapiro evaluations might subsume the specialized circulant consequence. Failed searches alone are not novelty certificates.

value.rationale: Rudin–Shapiro and complementary Golay polynomials are standard low-correlation digital filter families. For rational (in particular integer) two-channel mixing, complete invertibility/singular-kernel classification on every dyadic cycle is a natural deconvolution invariant, not an arbitrary sample parameter. Corank \(\le1\) uniformly in length, the exact parity-sensitive exceptional mixing directions, and the qualitative jump to \(\ge2\) lost modes for irrational real coefficients expose a substantive arithmetic boundary. No stability or wavelet basis theorem is claimed.
